ios.desc:
When you have thousands of photos and videos, finding and remembering the ones you love is not easy. Piqt fixes that, securely on your iPhone, without uploading a single one.

Find your best shots without scrolling through thousands. Piqt scores every photo on-device: sharpness, exposure, a model trained on 255,000 human-rated images, faces, and how rare the moment is. Then it surfaces what's actually worth keeping. Videos get their own on-device read too, sampled across frames and audio quality. Disagree with a score? See exactly why, and adjust it.

Your trips, found for you. Piqt notices when your photo habits change, spots your trips and big days, and names each one for where you actually went. Open a trip and the whole app follows: pick the best by score, walk it day by day in the trip's own time zone, and save the cut as an album in Photos that's ready to show off.

We all click the shutter 10 times when we're taking a selfie or a group picture. You don't need them all. Piqt groups the near-duplicates your Photos app misses, picks the sharpest, and lets you compare and swap in one glance.

Turn screenshot chaos into something searchable. Recipes, receipts, and saved ideas get filed automatically, with the useful details pulled out. The one you need is a search away, not 400 swipes back.

One scan, and Piqt keeps up from there. Piqt scans new photos and videos as they arrive, nothing gets redone for no reason.

Free to browse everything, forever, and your first batch of favorites is on us. Piqt Plus ($3.99/mo or $29.99/yr, both with a 7-day free trial, or $49.99 once) unlocks the rest: favoriting without limits, clearing, saving trips as albums, committing a video trim. Recovering anything you cleared is never gated, subscribed or not.

Nothing you do in Piqt is permanent. Cleared photos move to an album you can review, and the actual delete stays in Apple's own Photos app, in your hands. Video trims are non-destructive edits, reversible right from Photos itself.

Most of all, we care about your privacy. Everything is scanned on your device. Your photos and videos never get shipped off to a datacenter somewhere. No account, no upload, no exceptions.

This app is subject to the standard Apple Terms of Use (EULA): https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/

show_hn.title: Show HN: Piqt (iOS) – on device photo and video curator

quotes.text:
I've just released Piqt, an on-device photo/video curator. For years I've wanted to get my Apple Photos library under control, but there just aren't enough hours in the day. I started out in Jupyter notebooks to see how much I can use AI models to automate it and Piqt is the result.

My goals with Piqt:

- Fully on device: I use a number of ML models, Apple Vision API, clustering algorithms to rank and sort your photos. Everything runs on device.

- Private and Safe: Piqt has no accounts, no cloud services, no personal identifiers. Images or personal information never leave the device. Piqt also CAN'T delete your photos. I have a test and validation step in the release process to ensure no delete APIs exist in the code. Instead, Piqt stages things you want to clear out in an album, which you can delete when you're ready.

- A library you can use. I didn't just want to clean out images or clear up space. There are plenty of apps for this. My ultimate goal is to make your (and my) photos easier to navigate

I'm just looking for feedback on the app and the approach. I'd love to chat about the vision models I'm using and hear from you about any research or techniques I've missed.

App Store Link: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/piqt-photo-video-curator/id6778080898

Blog with detail on technical decisions: https://piqt.app/blog/piqt-design-values/
